scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Escalator steps appear from the floor, rise up, then vanish at the top. Where do the steps go?

scenes.name: loop
scenes.text: The steps are linked in one big loop, like a bicycle chain. They go up on top, and return upside down underneath.

scenes.name: motor
scenes.text: An electric motor at the top turns gears that pull the chain of steps around.

scenes.name: tracks
scenes.text: Each step has wheels on two tracks. The tracks change height, so steps stay flat and form stairs in the middle.

scenes.name: flatten
scenes.text: At the top and bottom, the tracks come together, so the steps flatten into a walkway for safe getting on and off.

scenes.name: handrail
scenes.text: The rubber handrail is a separate loop, driven to move at about the same speed as the steps.

scenes.name: safety
scenes.text: Sensors and an emergency stop button can halt the escalator, and comb plates stop things getting caught.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: A loop of steps, two tracks, one motor. Follow for more on how things really work.
